newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta shares end lower in blue-chip sell-off.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta shares end lower in blue-chip sell-off.

text.p: Jakarta share prices closed lower on Thursday on foreign selling of selected blue-chips despite a significant rise in market heavyweight Telkom, brokers said.
The Jakarta Composite Index fell 1.03 points, or 0.18 percent, to close at 571.26 points after hitting an intra-day high of 574.50 points in the morning session.
Gainers led losers by 56 to 51, with 49 counters unchanged.
Brokers said many operators were likely to continue on the sell side on Friday and forecast the index falling slightly as a correction after three days of gains continues.
"After gains for the last three days, the market seems to have lost interest. Technically, it's better to take profit," said one foreign broker.
"I think nothing much could happen tomorrow, it could be like today...lazy," said one local broker.
Telecommunications firm Telkom topped the active list with 7.5 million shares traded, rising 75 rupiah to 3,550. The volume was boosted by cross-trading transactions involving about 5 million shares.
Brokers said they could find no concrete reason for the rise, but said fresh buying from overseas triggered the gains.

Car producer Astra International traded unchanged at 3,750 rupiah on a turnover of 5.8 million shares after rising to 3,825 rupiah in the morning. Cross-trading in Astra was 33.6 million shares, or more than 50 percent of total cross-trading volume.
Satellite firm Indosat, cigarette maker Gudang Garam and cement producer Semen Gresik were among the targets of foreign profit-taking.
Glass and plastics manufacturer Igar Jaya fell 250 rupiah to 3,050 on a volume of 3.4 million shares on local-led profit taking.
